Container.Name: alcove
Container.Overview: A private, self-hosted place for a couple or a family to upload their Tryst backups and see, side by side, what they choose to share: a shared calendar, compare views and member cards, in spaces that only members can see. Encrypted at rest, no outside connections, for adults who have all agreed. Keep this on your LAN only; never forward the port to the internet.
Container.Requires: The data and backup folders must be writable by uid 65532, and the key file must exist before the first start (RUNBOOK section 1). Do not publish the port outside your LAN.

Config.Name: Web UI port
Config.Description: LAN only. Never forward this port to the internet.

Config.Name: Data
Config.Description: Uploads, photos and the sealed database. Only ciphertext is ever written here.

Config.Name: Key file
Config.Description: The one master key file, in its own folder (never inside the data folder) and owned by uid 65532, because the container cannot read the root-only flash drive. Make it once with the keygen command in the RUNBOOK, and keep a second copy somewhere else. If every copy is lost, the data cannot be recovered.

Config.Name: Backups
Config.Description: Instance backups (ciphertext only). Must not be inside the data folder. A different disk or a share is best.

Config.Name: Time zone for new people
Config.Description: A name like Europe/Berlin. Used for anyone who has not set their own on their profile. Empty means UTC.

Config.Name: Allowed networks
Config.Description: Optional, comma separated, for example 192.168.1.0/24. Empty means the private LAN ranges only. A value here beats the admin console (the way back in if you lock yourself out).

Config.Name: Backups to keep
Config.Description: How many of the newest instance backups a run keeps (never fewer than one).

Config.Name: Person's recovery window (days)
Config.Description: How long a person can restore something they deleted.

Config.Name: Administrator's recovery window (days)
Config.Description: How long the administrator can restore a deletion. Never shorter than the person's window.
